text.content:
Latin name: Via Humanitatis

Virtues: Conscience, Self-Control

Opposing the Road of the Beast, followers of the Via Humanitatis (Prodigals) believe that only by maintaining their hold on humanity can they survive the Beast's horrors. Humanity is not an accident of birth but the result of a feeling heart; one is truly dead only when that heart is corrupted or callused with uncaring. Prodigals cling to human society, interact with mortals, and pursue religion and old habits with fervor, committing smaller sins to forestall greater ones and seeking penance and redemption when they fail. Many @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} follow this road, and most Prodigals live near or among common folk, seeming little different from the mortals around them.

The Ethics:

  • A man is measured by his words, his deeds, and his heart, not his birth or circumstance.
  • The ability to reason separates man from beast.
  • Do unto others as you would have them do unto you. All men are brothers.
  • Freedom is earned with dignity and justice.

Aura of Conviction (Normalcy): Normalcy. Followers of Via Humanitatis don't project their aura so much as suppress the unease their supernatural form would normally inspire, working when they hide their supernatural selves and try to appear normal.

Hierarchy of Sins (most to least severe):

  1. Selfish thoughts; minor selfish acts.
  2. Injury to another person (deliberate or otherwise); theft and robbery.
  3. Accidental violation of another (e.g., drinking a vessel dry from starvation); wanton destruction.
  4. Impassioned violation of another (e.g., killing in frenzy); planned violation of another (e.g., murder).
  5. Casual violation of another (e.g., wanton killing, feeding past satiation); the most heinous and demented acts.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire, revised as The Long Night)
